Introduction

Despite being very happy with my Squape R (an understatement), I had the hardware itch (not the one you can go to the doctor for). I had had Russian 91%s, and really didn't want to go back to those. They're fine, but I think I'll be done with Kayfuns for a little bit. I had seen the Erlkoenigin come up some time ago, but it seemed like a lot was going on from the preproduction blueprints I had found, and it ended up being expensive. Then, due to a run-in with Sir Isaac Newton's Ghost, my Squape has been temporarily removed from the scene.

Then they made the Erlprinz. The Erlkoenigin's cheaper brother. Way cheaper. Like $100 cheaper. $50 for an authentic RTA? I can do that, if only to use for a little bit while I wait for my Squape R's replacement glass to come in. I pulled it from Vapor Shark's website, ponied up for the 2-Day shipping option from UPS, and $62 and three days (weekends, the bane of vapemail) it was on my door.

Impressions

Getting the build right is a little tricky. I found that using Japanese cotton and 8 wraps of 28AWG Kanthal around a 2.5mm bit (0.9 ohms) requires that I just barely stuff the ends into the channels. That leaves a lot of empty channel real estate, but I'm using max VG. It took a few tries to get it right, but it's just humping along.

It holds a lot of juice, and it fills up really quickly, thanks to its novel top-fill system. No leaks when I leave some space up top when I fill it up, and it's chuffing along like a champ.

Then there's the drip tip. The reason this will be a 2 part review. This. Fucking. Drip tip.

It screws into place, which is neat because that's how it manages its top fill and keeps the whole thing together. But because it uses a proprietary screwing system, that makes this damn thing unshareable if your friends want to give it a shot and you don't want their mouth herpes. And my biggest complaint is that I CAN TASTE THIS DRIP TIP. The taste invades EVERYTHING. I washed all the pieces before I started using it, and it's this cloying artificial taste that pervades every puff.

The drip tip is why this is a 2-part interview. I got this this afternoon and it took me a while to get the build right, and this drip tip is just really really driving me mad.

The last word on this one, is if you're thinking about it, hold off until I get another drip tip. Ffffuuuuuuucccckkkkkk.

[Question] Is there a way to customize the "x subscribers y users here now"?

There certainly is! The class handle for 'x subscribers' is .subscribers and the 'users here now' is .users-online. If you want to modify what it says, just use this code as a reference:

.subscribers .word {
 visibility: hidden;
}
.subscribers .word:before {
 visibility: visible;
 content: "voat goats";
}
.users-online .word {
 visibility: hidden;
}
.users-online .word:before {
 visibility: visible;
 content: "voat goats spectating";
}

Edit: this code doesn't work in Internet Explorer. Here is an updated tutorial on a solution that works in all browsers.

No fret! They're actually called CSS classes or IDs. Difference between the two is that IDs are clipped onto elements that are only used once (there's only one header on this site, so ID works best in that case), and classes are slapped onto reoccurring elements like comments or buttons. IDs use # and classes use . at the beginning of the class/ID name.

As for finding out what classes/IDs to modify, hit that F12 key (assuming you're using a modern, popular browser like Chrome, Firefox, IE, etc.). A pane should come rushing in. On said pane, you're going to see a button that (typically) looks like an arrow pointing to a box, called 'inspect element' or something of the sort. Click it. Then, just click on anything on the webpage and it'll point you toward that exact HTML tag with the appropriate CSS class/ID, if it has one.
